sentences.text: Lithornis is an extinct genus of paleognathous birds, a group that includes modern ratites and tinamous.
Despite its close relationship to modern flightless ratites and poor-flying tinamous, Lithornis was capable of good flight.
This bird possessed toe claws and reversed halluxes that allowed for efficient perching, a trait not found in modern tinamous.
Lithornis possessed wing bones similar to storks and vultures, enabling it to soar, unlike its modern tinamous relatives.
Lithornis had well-developed olfactory lobes suggesting a nocturnal, forest-dwelling lifestyle, while retaining large optical lobes common in flying birds.
A fossil egg attributed to Lithornis celetius has been identified.
The name Lithornis means 'stone bird' in ancient Greek, reflecting its early prominence in fossil bird discussions.
Richard Owen described the species Lithornis vulturinus in 1840 based on bones resembling those of vultures.
The type fossils of Lithornis vulturinus were collected from Early Eocene London Clay deposits on the Isle of Sheppey, Kent, England.
The original holotype fossil of Lithornis vulturinus was destroyed during bombing in World War II.
A neotype was designated in 1988 to replace the destroyed holotype, allowing researchers to diagnose the genus as a paleognath based on North American congeners.
The species Lithornis celetius was described by Peter Houde in 1988 from fossils found at Bangtail Quarry in Montana.
The species Lithornis hookeri was originally described as Pediorallus hookeri in 1984 before being transferred to the genus Lithornis.
The original fossil for Lithornis nasi was collected by W. George from the London Clay at Walton on the Naze, Essex, England.
Lithornis nasi was originally described as the rail Pediorallus nasi by Harrison in 1984 before being reclassified.
Lithornis promiscuus was described by Peter Houde in 1988 from the Willwood Formation in Wyoming, dating to the earliest Eocene.
Lithornis celetius was of average size for the genus, and its name references a race horse from the type locality.
Lithornis hookeri is the smallest species within the family Lithornithidae.
Lithornis belongs to the family Lithornithidae.
Some researchers classify the genus Calciavis as a species of Lithornis, specifically L. grandei.
Lithornis fossils are confirmed from the Upper Paleocene to the Middle Eocene, with a possible extension into the late Cretaceous.
Lithornis lived between 60.9 and 48.07 million years ago, from the Selandian to the Ypresian stages.
Lithornis celetius lived during the earliest Tiffanian stage of the Late Paleocene, as indicated by the Fort Union Formation.
It is debated whether Lithornis nasi is a distinct species or a junior synonym of L. vulturinus, with recent studies arguing for its distinctness based on size differences.
